extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning sheaf theory and foundations of algebraic geometry (readers of Ravi Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and exercises about presheaves, sheafification, stalks, sheaves on a base, monomorphisms/epimorphisms, abelian category structure of sheaves, and inverse image/pushforward functors — aimed at learning and proving the foundational statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution: stalkwise isomorphism does not imply sheaf isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: this question does not say that if two sheaves have isomorphic stalks, then they are isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware: isomorphism of stalks at all points need not give a global isomorphism of sheaves. Counterexamples exist; exercises and later remarks illustrate the phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf-counterexamples hint
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises 2.4.F (a)-(c) ask to show some earlier exercises are false for general presheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General hint: consider a 2-point space with the discrete topology to find counterexamples where presheaf statements fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification: universal property (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a presheaf on X, then a morphism of presheaves sh : F → F^sh on X is a sheafification of F if F^sh is a sheaf, and for any sheaf G, and any presheaf morphism g : F → G, there exists a unique morphism of sheaves f : F^sh → G making the diagram commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal property characterizes sheafification abstractly; any construction must verify it. Use the universal diagram to deduce uniqueness and functoriality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of sheafification
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that sheafification is unique up to unique isomorphism, assuming it exists. If F is a sheaf, then the sheafification is id : F → F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consequence of the universal property. Use uniqueness-from-universal-property standard arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification is functorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume sheafification exists. Use the universal property to show that for any morphism of presheaves φ : F → G, we get a natural induced morphism of sheaves φ^sh : F^sh → G^sh. Show that sheafification is a functor from presheaves on X to sheaves on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply universal property to the composite F → G → G^sh to produce the induced map; check compatibility and composition to get functoriality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete construction of sheafification (compatible germs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define F^sh(U) as the set of 'compatible germs' of the presheaf F over U: F^sh(U) := { (f_p ∈ F_p)_{p∈U} : for all p∈U, there exists an open neighborhood V of p contained in U, and s∈F(V) with s_q = f_q for all q∈V }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit description gives the sections of the sheafification as tuples of stalk elements that are locally represented by honest sections. Verify restriction maps are tautological.

rubrics_metrics.name: F^sh is a sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the presheaf U ↦ F^sh(U) (with tautological restriction maps) forms a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the local nature of the definition: compatibility of germs and local existence of representing sections give identity and gluability axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural map sh : F → F^sh
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural map of presheaves sh : F → F^sh sending a section to its family of germs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe this map explicitly and check it respects restrictions; use it to connect the presheaf with its sheafification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification satisfies universal property (verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the concrete map sh : F → F^sh satisfies the universal property of sheafification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given any map F → G with G a sheaf, demonstrate there is a unique map F^sh → G compatible with sh by sending a compatible-germs section to the locally defined values in G; uniqueness follows from stalk-determinacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification is left adjoint to forgetful functor
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheafification functor is left-adjoint to the forgetful functor from sheaves on X to presheaves on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restatement of the universal property as an adjunction; consequences include understanding when sheafification is needed (e.g., cokernels) and not needed (e.g., kernels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification induces isomorphism on stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: The canonical map F → F^sh induces an isomorphism of stalks F_p → (F^sh)_p for all p∈X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the concrete description of stalks via colimits and the local nature of F^sh; adjointness can also give a conceptual proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification of constant presheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reality check: the sheafification of a constant presheaf is the corresponding constant sheaf. (If X is a topological space and S is a set, then (S^pre)^sh may be naturally identified with the constant sheaf associated to S.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify by comparing sections and stalks; use Exercise 2.2.10 as reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Espace étalé / space-of-sections viewpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'space of sections' (espace étalé) construction yields a different-sounding but essentially identical description of sheafification: the sheaf of sections of the espace étalé of a presheaf is its sheafification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This perspective can be preferred by some readers; compare Construction 2.4.7 and Exercise 2.2.E to see equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of monomorphisms of sheaves (subsheaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose φ : F → G is a morphism of sheaves of sets on a topological space X. The following are equivalent: (a) φ is a monomorphism in the category of sheaves. (b) φ is injective on the level of stalks: φ_p : F_p → G_p is injective for all p∈X. (c) φ is injective on the level of open sets: φ(U) : F(U) → G(U) is injective for all open U⊂X. If these hold, F is a subsheaf of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that morphisms are determined by stalks for (b)⇒(a), and an 'indicator sheaf' trick for (a)⇒(c). The statement generalizes to sheaves valued in other categories replacing 'injective' by 'monomorphism'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of epimorphisms of sheaves (quotient sheaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose φ : F → G is a morphism of sheaves of sets on X. The following are equivalent: (a) φ is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves. (b) φ is surjective on the level of stalks: φ_p : F_p → G_p is surjective for all p∈X. If these hold, G is a quotient sheaf of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use skyscraper sheaves for the (b)⇒(a) direction. Note: surjectivity on all open sets is not equivalent to being an epimorphism (there is no (c) analogous to monomorphism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local vs global surjectivity caution (exponential example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: On X = C, the exponential map exp : O_X → O_X^* describes O_X^* as a quotient sheaf of O_X, but there exist open sets on which the map is not surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows the sheaf notion of surjectivity is stalkwise/local: nowhere-vanishing holomorphic functions have local logarithms (local surjectivity) but may lack a global logarithm (global non-surjectivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base of topology and sheaf on a base (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf on a base {B_i} consists of sets F(B_i) for each B_i in the base and restriction maps res_{B_j,B_i} satisfying presheaf composition axioms, together with the base identity axiom and base gluability axiom: identity — sections over B determined by restrictions to basic opens; gluability — compatible sections on a cover by basic opens glue to a unique section on the union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encodes the minimal data on a base needed to recover the full sheaf. Keep the identity and gluability axioms explicit when constructing or checking a sheaf from base data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering a sheaf from its restriction to a base (existence and uniqueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.5.1: Suppose {B_i} is a base on X, and F is a sheaf of sets on this base. Then there is a sheaf F extending F (with isomorphisms F(B_i) ≅ F(B_i) agreeing with restriction maps). This sheaf F is unique up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct F as the sheaf of compatible germs built from the base sections; verify the natural maps give isomorphisms on basic opens and check uniqueness from universal/stalk considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks from a base (colimit description)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a presheaf F on a base, define the stalk at p by F_p = colim_{B_i ∋ p} F(B_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this colimit description to compute stalks when only base data is available; it feeds into the compatible-germs construction for the extended sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms correspond between sheaves and sheaves-on-a-base
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of sheaves on the base is a collection of maps F(B_k) → G(B_k) commuting with restriction maps. (a) A morphism of sheaves is determined by the induced morphism on the base. (b) A morphism of sheaves on the base gives a morphism of the induced sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To define or check morphisms globally, it suffices to specify them on a base subject to compatibility; conversely, global morphisms restrict to the base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of categories: sheaves vs sheaves on a base
rubrics_metrics.description: Remark: the constructions describe an equivalence of categories between sheaves on X and sheaves on a given base of X (up to canonical isomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think functorially: restriction to the base and extension-by-compatible-germs give quasi-inverse functors, though compositions need not be strictly the identity on the nose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing sheaves from local data (cocycle condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} is an open cover of X and we have sheaves F_i on U_i with isomorphisms φ_{ij} : F_i|_{U_i∩U_j} ≅ F_j|_{U_i∩U_j} satisfying the cocycle condition (φ_{jk} ∘ φ_{ij} = φ_{ik} on triple overlaps), then the F_i glue to a sheaf F on X unique up to unique isomorphism with F|_{U_i} ≅ F_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume finiteness of the cover — use base-of-opens contained in some U_i for construction. The hypothesis φ_{ii}=id follows from the cocycle condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient criterion for epimorphism via base-surjectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a morphism of sheaves F → G on a base {B_i} is surjective for all B_i (i.e., F(B_i) → G(B_i) is surjective for all i), then the corresponding morphism of sheaves is an epimorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a practical sufficient condition for surjectivity; the converse need not hold, see exponential example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaves of abelian groups form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.6.2: Sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space X form an abelian category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show kernels and cokernels exist and can be checked on stalks (kernels already sheaves; cokernels: take presheaf cokernel then sheafify). Many abelian-categorical properties reduce to checking on stalks (where they are just abelian groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of kernel and cokernel equal kernel/cokernel of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.A and 2.6.B: For a morphism φ : F → G of sheaves of abelian groups, (ker φ)_p ≅ ker(F_p → G_p) and (coker φ)_p ≅ coker(F_p → G_p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local descriptions and the fact that sheafification preserves stalks to prove these identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image sheaf is sheafification of image presheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.C: The image sheaf im φ is the sheafification of the image presheaf; the stalk of the image is the image of the stalks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an abelian category sense, define image by kernel of cokernel; concretely, sheafify the presheaf-image to get the sheaf-image and check stalkwise equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk functor is exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Important Exercise 2.6.D: Taking the stalk at a point p defines an exact functor Ab_X → Ab (i.e., stalks preserve exact sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since exactness of sheaves can be checked stalkwise, use the stalk-colimit description to verify exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections-over-U is left-exact but not exact in general
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.F: For an exact sequence 0 → F → G → H of sheaves of abelian groups and an open U⊂X, the sequence 0 → F(U) → G(U) → H(U) is exact; but the functor Γ(U,−) need not be exact (i.e., right-exactness can fail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counterexamples such as the exponential exact sequence to show failure of surjectivity on global sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward is left-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.G: If 0 → F → G → H is exact on X and π : X → Y is continuous, then 0 → π_*F → π_*G → π_*H is exact on Y (i.e., π_* is left-exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret global sections as pushforward to a point; use left-exactness pointwise or stalkwise as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom functors left-exactness properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.H: For sheaves of abelian groups, Hom(·,F) is a left-exact covariant functor Ab_X → Ab and Hom(F,·) is a left-exact contravariant functor Ab_X → Ab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to corresponding statements for abelian groups on stalks and use exactness of stalk functor.

rubrics_metrics.name: OX-modules form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.6.I and remarks: If (X,O_X) is a ringed space, then O_X-modules form an abelian category; many sheaf-theoretic abelian statements carry over with minimal change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check underlying sheaves of abelian groups for exactness and abelian properties; many prior exercises adapt to O_X-modules verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of OX-modules: construction and stalk property
rubrics_metrics.description: Important Exercise 2.6.J: (a) Define tensor product of two O_X-modules categorically; give an explicit construction: take the presheaf tensor product and sheafify. (b) Show (M ⊗_{O_X} N)_p ≅ M_p ⊗_{O_{X,p}} N_p (tensor product of stalks is stalk of tensor product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheafification may be necessary for the presheaf tensor to become a sheaf; use stalk computations and colimit properties to show stalkwise equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse image (pullback) sheaf defined by adjoint or construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 2.7.1 and Construction 2.7.2: For a continuous map π : X → Y, define π^{-1} as the left adjoint to π_*; concretely define π^{-1}_{pre}G(U) = lim_{V ⊃ π(U)} G(V) (colimit over opens V of Y containing π(U)), and then set π^{-1}G := (π^{-1}_{pre}G)^sh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presheaf π^{-1}_{pre} need not be a sheaf, so sheafify. Use the adjunction property as the defining universal criterion for π^{-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction: π^{-1} left-adjoint to π_*
rubrics_metrics.description: Important Exercise 2.7.B: For π : X → Y continuous, there is a natural bijection Mor_X(π^{-1}G, F) ↔ Mor_Y(G, π_*F), natural in F and G; explicit description via compatible collections φ_{V,U} commuting with restriction diagrams is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove adjointness by constructing the bijection and checking naturality; the compatible-collection description is a hands-on alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of inverse image: (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_{π(p)}
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.7.C: If π(p)=q, there is a natural isomorphism (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colimit descriptions of stalks and preservation of stalks by sheafification, or deduce from adjointness. This identification underlies many intuitive pictures of pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction via inverse image for open inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.7.D: If i : U ↪ Y is inclusion of an open subset and G a sheaf on Y, then i^{-1}G is naturally isomorphic to the restriction G|_U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case of inverse image; check definitions to see that colimits over opens containing i(U)=U recover sections on U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse image is exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.7.E: The functor π^{-1} is exact from sheaves of abelian groups on Y to sheaves of abelian groups on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness can be checked on stalks, and by (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_{π(p)} exactness follows; alternatively use left-adjointness and filtered colimit exactness for abelian groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a sheaf (definition and basic property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise/Definition 2.7.F: Define Supp G := { p∈Y : |G_p| ≠ 1 } (for set-valued sheaves; for abelian groups, support = { p : G_p ≠ 0 }). If Supp G ⊂ Z closed and i : Z ↪ Y the inclusion, then the natural map i_*i^{-1}G → G is an isomorphism (a sheaf supported on a closed subset can be considered a sheaf on that closed subset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is the locus where stalks are non-final; use this to restrict attention or identify sheaves supported on closed subsets as sheaves on that subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by zero i_! for open inclusion and its properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 2.7.G: For i : U ↪ Y open inclusion define i_{pre,!}F(W)=F(W) if W⊂U and 0 otherwise, then i_! = (i_{pre,!}F)^sh. Properties: (a) i_{pre,!} need not be a sheaf; (b) (i_!F)_q = F_q if q∈U and 0 otherwise; (c) i_! is exact; (d) there is a natural inclusion i_! i^{-1}G → G and a short exact sequence 0 → i_! i^{-1}G → G → j_* j^{-1}G → 0 when j is inclusion of complement Z; (e) (i_!, i^{-1}) form an adjoint pair: Hom_Y(i_!F, G) ≅ Hom_U(F, G|_U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sheafification to remedy presheaf shortcomings; compute stalks directly; adjunction identifies sections over U with Hom(i_! O_U, G).
